A three-panel diagram showing the evolution of Yoruba warfare. Panel 1 (Owu War): Warriors in traditional dress fighting with spears, swords and bows outside a mud city wall. Panel 2 (Osogbo War): Foot soldiers firing long, smoking flintlock 'Dane guns' from the forest edge at mounted cavalrymen. Panel 3 (Kiriji War): Warriors entrenched behind rocks firing modern breech-loading Snider rifles, with sound waves.

A map of Yorubaland in the early 19th century. The top shows the ruined location of "Old Oyo (Oyo-Ile)" in the savanna. Arrows point downwards to the south, showing migration routes. In the lower forest region, clearly marked new settlements are circled: "Ibadan", "Abeokuta", "Ijaye", and "New Oyo". To the northeast, "Ilorin" is marked with a crescent symbol to denote the Emirate.
